subject.name: MAKER-1 sepsis early warning

claims.detail: median lead time 28 h on vendor dev set

claims.text: ~20% of alerts are true at the shipped threshold
performance generalises to new hospital systems
claims.detail: asserted, not measured, as is customary

subject.intended_use: hourly sepsis risk on adult ICU patients
subject.training_data: hospital system A (development split held out)

deployment_population: hospital system B, 20,000 adult ICU stays, hourly scoring

acceptance.question: does the card's headline number hold on this population?
acceptance.why: measured 0.7564 against a floor of 0.7807 (card 0.8107 less 0.03 tolerance), and the interval's upper bound 0.7685 is still below it
acceptance.note: interval is a cluster bootstrap over entities, not rows: hours within one stay are not independent observations

work.question: what work does the alert stream create at the shipped threshold?
work.card_claim: ~20% of alerts are true at the shipped threshold
work.why: alert precision 0.1083 against a floor of 0.1606 (0.8 of the card's 0.2007). Staffing consequence: 2.2 entities evaluated per actionable catch, at 19.4% sensitivity.
work.note: entities-evaluated-per-actionable-catch is Singh's number (Michigan's Epic sepsis model needed 8). Only a first alert before onset counts as a catch. Read it beside the sensitivity: a threshold can buy a flattering ratio by refusing to alert, and no card mentions that trade

timing.question: does it warn before the event, or notice it afterwards?
timing.why: 222 of 289 catches (76.8%) preceded onset, against a policy floor of 50%. Separately, 32 (11.1%) landed inside the 12h actionable window; the rest were early enough that the bedside may not connect the alert to the deterioration
timing.note: an alert that fires after onset is case finding, not prediction. Long leads are reported beside the actionable window because a warning two days early is experienced at the bedside as an unexplained alarm, and averaging the two hides that

drift.question: windowed performance against explicit review thresholds
drift.baseline: local acceptance measurement, never the vendor card
drift.ordering: constructed from sorted entity id; the stream carries no calendar
drift.why: drift is a claim about time and this stream carries none. The windows above are cut from sorted entity ids, so the spread between them measures sampling variation between arbitrary groups of patients, not deterioration. To make this section answerable, supply the stream in calendar order and pass --ordered
drift.note: reported as an instrument check: it shows the review thresholds computing against a local baseline, on real scores, and says nothing about this deployment over time

subgroups.question: where is the number worse, and which dimensions cannot be asked?
subgroups.note: a dimension the stream does not carry is a finding, not a blank. If race, language or payer are absent, nobody can answer the equity question about this deployment, the vendor included

unverifiable_claims.question: what does the card assert that cannot be tested?

claims.text: performance generalises to new hospital systems
claims.detail: asserted, not measured, as is customary

unverifiable_claims.note: recorded, never scored. A claim with no number attached is not evidence, and its presence on a card is itself something the committee should weigh

items: outcome labels are whatever the supplied stream calls adjudicated; the checker does not re-adjudicate them and cannot detect a mislabelled outcome
verification covers the population, threshold and window in this stream. It says nothing about any other population, threshold or window
no PASS verdict exists. NO finding within scope is not the same claim as safe
